accuracy.reason: CAP-scope, network-partition, linearizable-consistency and cap-availability match Gilbert/Lynch formal definitions, including real-time order and unbounded eventual termination. No product-wide or error-response shortcut is claimed.

evidence.quote: Linearizability: operations behave as if they take effect in a single order that respects real time.

mechanisms.reason: Impossibility-mechanism derives the information barrier and rules out guessing or blocking the other operation as an escape. Favor-consistency and favor-availability explain allowed work and reconciliation consequences.

evidence.quote: Guessing the new value cannot guarantee correctness across possible unseen writes.

coherence.reason: All nine objectives progress from definitions to proof, operating alternatives, conditional convergence and per-operation choices. Diagram explicitly scopes majority behavior to a majority agreement protocol; no unsafe generic quorum guarantee. Shared presentation inspected, not executed.

evidence.quote: In a three-server system using a majority-based agreement protocol, two servers must agree before a write completes.

decisions.reason: Eventual-convergence and operation-level-decision cover staleness, lost conflicting intent, recovery and unaffected operations. The lesson separates normal latency/cost decisions from the theorem.

evidence.quote: It does not predict normal-operation latency, capacity or operating cost; evaluate those separately.

clarity.reason: Definitions, numerical counterexample and user-visible examples make the real-time and convergence distinctions accessible without assuming consensus implementation expertise.

evidence.quote: Eventually gives no fixed deadline or immediate read-your-writes guarantee.

outcomes.reason: All scope criteria supported: learner explains networked copies, partition without crash, partition-tolerance scope and why choosing two universally or ignoring communication failures is invalid.

All six criteria supported: single valid real-time order, later read and overlapping operations, eventual/ACID distinction, per-request eventual completion without latency bound, refusal/error consequence and uptime distinction.
All three criteria supported: B lacks information, must reflect completed 1, old value breaks consistency, indefinite wait/refusal breaks availability, guessing cannot work across unseen values.

All six criteria supported: restrict unsafe operations while coordinated ones continue, failure/delay cost, local stale replies, conflicting writes requiring resolution, and no automatic preservation of intent or cross-record rules.

All six criteria supported: convergence conditions, no deadline/read-your-writes, intent-loss distinction, strict versus stale-tolerant choices, visible failure/staleness and recovery policy, per-operation configuration and separate normal performance evaluation.
